questions.question: What causes kwashiorkor and marasmus, and how are they different?
questions.expected_answer: Kwashiorkor is caused by a lack of protein; the child has a swollen belly, legs and face from water building up, thin, discoloured hair and peeling skin. Marasmus is caused by a lack of food in general, so not enough energy or protein; the child is extremely thin, with bones showing and very little fat or muscle. Both are prevented by a balanced diet with enough energy food and protein.

questions.question: Name three deficiency diseases caused by a lack of a vitamin or mineral, and a food that prevents each one.
questions.expected_answer: Scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C and prevented by citrus fruit, guavas, tomatoes or cabbage. Rickets is caused by a lack of vitamin D or calcium and prevented by sunlight and milk or maas. Anaemia is caused by a lack of iron and prevented by red meat, beans or spinach. Night blindness is caused by a lack of vitamin A and prevented by carrots, butternut or sweet potatoes.

questions.question: Which diseases can be caused by eating too much sugar, salt or fat?
questions.expected_answer: Too much sugar can cause tooth decay and, with too much fat and too little exercise, obesity and type 2 diabetes. Too much salt over many years can cause high blood pressure, which can lead to heart attacks and strokes. Obesity can also cause problems with the heart, joints and breathing.
